307/2025.title: Transport Forum: November 2025, item 4
307/2025.description: Council’s decision on item 4 from the November 2025 Local Transport Forum.
307/2025.decisionSummary: Council adopts the recommendation for item 4 of the Local Transport Forum.

305/2025.title: Transport Forum recommendations: November 2025
305/2025.description: Council’s decisions on recommendations from the November 2025 Local Transport Forum.
305/2025.decisionSummary: Council adopts the recommendations from the 18 November 2025 Local Transport Forum, except items 2 and 4.

302/2025.title: Dunois Reserve watercraft storage
302/2025.description: A storage design for watercraft at Dunois Reserve, Longueville, and a wider strategy for managing watercraft.
302/2025.decisionSummary: Council adopts the concept design for Dunois Reserve watercraft storage. It agrees to build the storage while developing a watercraft management strategy for the whole council area.

299/2025.title: Rotary Peace Poles
299/2025.description: A proposal for five Peace Poles, with community input on their location and design.
299/2025.decisionSummary: Council supports Rotary Lane Cove’s Peace Poles project in principle and approves consultation on location and design. Installation of five poles depends on that consultation.

296/2025.title: Centrehouse committee representative
296/2025.description: Councillor representation on the Centrehouse management committee.
296/2025.decisionSummary: Council appoints Councillor Little as its primary Centrehouse management committee representative while Councillor Kennedy is president, or until September 2026.

293/2025.title: Council meeting rules
293/2025.description: The Code of Meeting Practice sets the rules for conducting Council meetings.
293/2025.decisionSummary: Council adopts the Code of Meeting Practice after removing clause 15.16 about expulsion from meetings. The code is to be published and take effect on 1 January 2026.

290/2025.short: Market Square report and building services
290/2025.title: Market Square report and building services
290/2025.description: Council’s response to the Market Square report, including ongoing air-conditioning and toilet issues.
290/2025.decisionSummary: Council receives the Market Square report and notes that air-conditioning and toilet issues are being addressed. Updates are to be included in the weekly councillor bulletin.

287/2025.title: Domestic and family violence prevention
287/2025.description: Council’s proposed work on domestic and family violence prevention, staff training and information for residents.
287/2025.decisionSummary: Council seeks advice from Local Government NSW about available support. Staff are to report in early 2026 on implementing the state prevention framework, with budgets for staff training and a community resource publication.

283/2025.title: Dog park repairs and maintenance
283/2025.description: Proposed improvements to drainage, surfaces, fencing and maintenance at Lane Cove dog parks.
283/2025.decisionSummary: Council requests cost estimates for dog park improvements before finalising the 2026/27 budget, including Blackman drainage and removal of dumped material at Turrumburra. It also asks staff to investigate safe shovel storage for filling holes at Blackman.

281/2025.title: Proposed school bus service cuts
281/2025.description: Council’s response to proposed cuts to local school bus services.
281/2025.decisionSummary: Council agrees to write to transport authorities and the local MP seeking service-use data, consultation and a delay to proposed school bus cuts. It repeats its call for the Region 7 bus network to return to public ownership when the lease ends, or earlier if feasible.

256/2025.title: Strata managing agent oversight
256/2025.description: A review of proposed reforms to accountability and oversight of strata managing agents.
256/2025.decisionSummary: Council defers the item to assess whether proposed NSW strata legislation addresses the suggested reforms. The matter is to return by March 2026.

271/2025.short: Pedestrian access and mobility plan consultation
271/2025.title: Pedestrian access and mobility plan consultation
271/2025.description: Community consultation on the draft 2025 Pedestrian Access and Mobility Plan.
271/2025.decisionSummary: Council places the draft Pedestrian Access and Mobility Plan on public exhibition for six weeks, with the results to be reported back.

267/2025.title: Children and Families Strategy consultation
267/2025.description: Community consultation on the draft Children and Families Strategy.
267/2025.decisionSummary: Council places the draft Children and Families Strategy on public exhibition for six weeks, with the results to be reported back.

259/2025.short: Galuwa food, beverage and events operator
259/2025.title: Galuwa food, beverage and events operator
259/2025.description: Proposed food, beverage and events arrangements and lease changes at Galuwa Recreation Centre.
259/2025.decisionSummary: Council endorses Lusso Kitchen as the preferred food, beverage and events operator and approves public exhibition of the relevant leases. The General Manager may sign if no submissions are received; otherwise a further report is required.

253/2025.short: Community safety information and crime reports
253/2025.title: Community safety information and crime reports
253/2025.description: Practical safety information for residents and businesses, and reports on local crime trends.
253/2025.decisionSummary: Council asks the General Manager to provide practical safety reminders during periods of increased property and parcel theft. It also requests a brief report after each police Community Safety Precinct Committee meeting on local crime trends and recommended initiatives.

251/2025.short: Sera Street car park access and safety
251/2025.title: Sera Street car park access and safety
251/2025.description: Pedestrian safety and access between Sera Street car park and Luz All Abilities.
251/2025.decisionSummary: Council agrees to refresh crossing markings, assess lighting, increase path cleaning and investigate replacing the handrail. It also requests a report on arrangements allowing businesses to lease nearby timed parking.

234/2025.short: Naming a new St Leonards South road
234/2025.title: Naming a new St Leonards South road
234/2025.description: Community suggestions for a new road between Berry Road and Park Road in St Leonards South.
234/2025.decisionSummary: Council seeks community suggestions for the new road’s name over six weeks, with the results to be reported back.

223/2025.short: Electric heating for Lane Cove Aquatic Centre
223/2025.title: Electric heating for Lane Cove Aquatic Centre
223/2025.description: Options for replacing gas heating at Lane Cove Aquatic Centre with electric heating.
223/2025.decisionSummary: Council requests a workshop on costs, emissions and timing for electrifying the pools and spa. The findings are to return for consideration in the 2026/27 budget and long-term financial plan.

219/2025.title: River Road pedestrian crossing
219/2025.description: A proposed safe crossing of River Road for St Leonards South residents and other pedestrians.
219/2025.decisionSummary: Council seeks urgent discussions with Transport for NSW and other authorities on funding a safe River Road crossing, with a report by February 2026. It also seeks a joint council approach to the transport projects in the 2024 Crows Nest transport note.

201/2025.title: Planning agreement: 2–4 Pacific Highway
201/2025.description: A draft planning agreement associated with development at 2–4 Pacific Highway, St Leonards.
201/2025.decisionSummary: Council places the draft planning agreement and supporting documents on public exhibition alongside the development application. A report on the consultation results is to follow.

196/2025.title: Pride Month drag performance grants
196/2025.description: A proposed pilot grant program for local hospitality venues to host professional drag performers during Pride Month.
196/2025.decisionSummary: Council establishes a proposed pilot grant program of up to $5,000 for Pride Month in June 2026, funded from the social inclusion budget. It requires 28 days’ public notice and a further report before approval and promotion.

184/2025.short: July traffic decisions and Northwood parking
184/2025.title: July traffic decisions and Northwood parking
184/2025.description: Traffic Committee recommendations and parking arrangements around Fleming Street and Northwood Road.
184/2025.decisionSummary: Council adopts the July 2025 Traffic Committee recommendations except item 8. It agrees to investigate construction-period parking measures for Fleming Street and consult nearby residents about parking after Galuwa Recreation Centre opens fully.

145/2025.title: Canberra Avenue road closure timing
145/2025.description: The proposed timing and trial arrangements for closing part of Canberra Avenue in St Leonards South.
145/2025.decisionSummary: Council intends to keep Canberra Avenue open until a year after specified developments receive occupancy certificates, then trial a partial closure for a year before reviewing it. The General Manager is to negotiate the required planning agreement changes and report back.

158/2025.title: Local Environmental Plan review
158/2025.description: Proposed planning changes, including conservation zoning at 15 Centennial Avenue and a study of neighbourhood shops in Lane Cove North.
158/2025.decisionSummary: Council supports the planning proposal, including C2 zoning for 15 Centennial Avenue, and seeks state Gateway approval. It also requests a Lane Cove North neighbourhood shop study and invites Willoughby Council to participate without delaying the planning proposal.

148/2025.title: Review of community consultation
148/2025.description: A review of how Council consults residents and reports the effect of their feedback.
148/2025.decisionSummary: Council agrees to review its engagement strategy, including early input, accessibility, advisory committees and reporting of feedback. It will seek community feedback on its engagement documents, compare other councils’ approaches and report on staffing and resources.

112/2025.short: Council property leases and rental assistance
112/2025.title: Council property leases and rental assistance
112/2025.description: Proposed policies for leasing Council property and providing rental assistance.
112/2025.decisionSummary: Council agrees to exhibit the leasing and rental assistance policies. Before consultation, the leasing policy is to include climate requirements covering no new gas, phasing out existing gas, solar and batteries, and water-sensitive works.

257/2024.short: Return and Earn machine in St Leonards
257/2024.title: Return and Earn machine in St Leonards
257/2024.description: A request for an additional Return and Earn reverse vending machine in the St Leonards area.
257/2024.decisionSummary: Council agrees to ask Tomra for a St Leonards machine and seek support from North Sydney and Willoughby mayors. Subject to that response, it will investigate locations and report back.

254/2024.title: Karilla Avenue traffic study
254/2024.description: A proposed study to test whether Karilla Avenue traffic calming reduces through-traffic.
254/2024.decisionSummary: Council agrees to consider funding a traffic study and conduct it within 12 months of installing the traffic calming measures. The study should compare with 2015/16 results, avoid school holidays and identify further options if through-traffic has not fallen significantly.

204/2024.title: Morrice Street drainage reserve sale
204/2024.description: The proposed sale or lease of drainage reserve land near Morrice Street and Tambourine Bay Road.
204/2024.decisionSummary: Council agrees to sell reserve land to respondents accepting its terms at $2,000 per square metre plus administrative costs. Other occupiers must remove structures and restore boundaries or enter a lease, with the General Manager authorised to sign the documents.

279/2023.title: Destruction of endangered ecological communities
279/2023.description: Council’s investigation and proposed enforcement response to destruction of protected habitat.
279/2023.decisionSummary: Council asks staff to continue investigating and take enforcement action consistent with legal advice and its enforcement policy. It also agrees to seek stronger state penalties and take suitable action to obscure any view gained from the habitat destruction.

35/2026.short: Minor civil works and line marking contractors
35/2026.title: Minor civil works and line marking contractors
35/2026.description: Contractor panels for minor civil works, associated services and line marking.
35/2026.decisionSummary: Council appoints eight contractors for minor civil works and two for line marking. The panels run for three years, with two optional one-year extensions, and the General Manager may sign the documents.

33/2026.title: Tree maintenance contractor panel
33/2026.description: A contractor panel for tree pruning, tree removal and stump grinding services.
33/2026.decisionSummary: Council establishes a panel of ten tree maintenance suppliers for an initial three years, with two optional one-year extensions. The General Manager is authorised to sign the documents.

30/2026.short: Blackman and Turrumburra dog park improvements
30/2026.title: Blackman and Turrumburra dog park improvements
30/2026.description: Proposed improvement works at Blackman Park and Turrumburra off-leash dog areas.
30/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to consider Blackman Park dog area improvements in the draft 2026/27 budget. It endorses the recommended Turrumburra dog area works for 2025/26.

28/2026.title: 3 Austin Crescent heritage planning proposal
28/2026.description: A heritage planning proposal concerning 3 Austin Crescent, Lane Cove.
28/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses the planning proposal for referral to the NSW planning department for Gateway approval. Consultation is to follow the Gateway requirements, and previous submitters are to be advised.

26/2026.short: Council submission on the Draft Sydney Plan
26/2026.title: Council submission on the Draft Sydney Plan
26/2026.description: Council’s response to the NSW Government’s Draft Sydney Plan.
26/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses its draft submission on the Draft Sydney Plan and agrees to send it to the NSW planning department.

24/2026.title: Sustainability Action Plan consultation
24/2026.description: Consultation on the 2026–2030 Sustainability Action Plan and the results of the 2022–2025 plan.
24/2026.decisionSummary: Council places both draft sustainability documents on exhibition for 28 days. Before consultation, the new plan must include a breakdown of Sustainability Levy spending against the previous plan’s 12 goals.

22/2026.short: Music and arts economy inquiry submission
22/2026.title: Music and arts economy inquiry submission
22/2026.description: Council’s submission to the NSW parliamentary inquiry into the music and arts economy.
22/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses its submission to the NSW parliamentary inquiry into the music and arts economy. The General Manager is authorised to finalise and submit it.

20/2026.short: Council response to the Bondi Beach attack
20/2026.title: Council response to the Bondi Beach attack
20/2026.description: Council’s response to the December 2025 Bondi Beach attack and support for affected communities.
20/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes its response to the Bondi Beach attack and agrees to sign the Multicultural NSW pledge supporting Jewish Australians and opposing antisemitism.

15/2026.title: Public and community forum rules
15/2026.description: Rules and meeting times for residents speaking at Council’s public and community forums.
15/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts amended forum guidelines, including separate opportunities for agenda items and other matters. From March 2026, Council meetings begin at 7 pm and public forums take place at 7 pm on the preceding Monday; refused speaking applications require written reasons.

11/2026.title: Independent governance review
11/2026.description: An independent review of Council’s governance, oversight and internal controls.
11/2026.decisionSummary: Council approves an independent Governance Health Check covering governance effectiveness, compliance and responses to earlier oversight recommendations. The consultant’s findings, recommendations and any implementation plan are to be reported back.

9/2026.title: Council service review framework
9/2026.description: A framework and annual program for reviewing Council services.
9/2026.decisionSummary: Council receives the Service Review Framework and notes that the annual service review program will begin on 1 July 2026.

5/2026.short: Australia Day honour for Prem Ramburuth
5/2026.title: Australia Day honour for Prem Ramburuth
5/2026.description: Recognition of Lane Cove resident Emeritus Professor Prem Ramburuth’s 2026 Australia Day honour.
5/2026.decisionSummary: Council acknowledges Emeritus Professor Prem Ramburuth’s Australia Day honour and agrees to write with congratulations and thanks for their community contribution.

62/2026.title: Local Planning Panel expert appointment
62/2026.description: A change to the independent expert membership of the Lane Cove Local Planning Panel.
62/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes Clare Swan’s resignation and agrees to thank her. It appoints Brian Kirk as an independent expert member and will advise the NSW planning department of the change.

59/2026.short: Lane Cove North neighbourhood shops study
59/2026.title: Lane Cove North neighbourhood shops study
59/2026.description: Further studies and funding discussions about a possible neighbourhood centre in Lane Cove North.
59/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to ask Microsoft and other potential developers about including a neighbourhood centre in development proposals. It will seek shared funding for the studies from state and federal representatives and agencies, then report on the responses and next steps.

57/2026.title: Domestic violence prevention training
57/2026.description: Participation in Local Government NSW’s domestic violence prevention training and a community resource publication.
57/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses training for interested councillors and relevant staff, with up to $17,010 allocated for 2026/27. It also notes budget provision for an online and printed domestic, family and sexual violence resource publication.

55/2026.title: Regional council organisation membership
55/2026.description: Council’s choice of regional council organisation.
55/2026.decisionSummary: Council reaffirms its Northern Sydney Regional Organisation of Councils membership. It agrees to tell the Minister and Office of Local Government that it declines membership of a Joint Organisation.

53/2026.short: Lane Cove North 40 km/h works and Karilla markings
53/2026.title: Lane Cove North 40 km/h works and Karilla markings
53/2026.description: Road markings and traffic calming required for the Lane Cove North 40 km/h plan, including Karilla Avenue.
53/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts the revised transport recommendations and agrees to install the Karilla Avenue markings required by Transport for NSW. It confirms a review of the traffic calming measures, including a traffic study within 12 months of installation and assessment of unintended effects.

48/2026.short: Salvaging tree logs for wildlife habitat
48/2026.title: Salvaging tree logs for wildlife habitat
48/2026.description: A proposed program to reuse hollow sections of fallen or removed trees as wildlife habitat.
48/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to investigate salvaging hollow logs through its tree maintenance program for wildlife habitat, including residential streets away from bushland. A report within three months is to cover feasibility, costs, safety, demand and links to the Backyard Habitat Program.

46/2026.title: Plaza outdoor dining maintenance
46/2026.description: Repairs, maintenance and weather protection for infrastructure used by Plaza outdoor dining tenants.
46/2026.decisionSummary: Council asks staff to meet outdoor dining tenants and prepare a maintenance plan covering repairs, costs, timing, after-hours contractors and rain protection. A report is to be provided through the weekly councillor bulletin within two months.

44/2026.short: Council revenue managed by third parties
44/2026.title: Council revenue managed by third parties
44/2026.description: A review of third-party revenue arrangements, including Market Square advertising panels.
44/2026.decisionSummary: Council requests a report within three months on revenue, contracts, oversight and risks in third-party arrangements, including Market Square advertising panels. The review excludes bus shelter advertising, recreation facility management and parking operations.

40/2026.title: Clean Up Australia Day volunteers
40/2026.description: Recognition of volunteers who helped clean up Lane Cove during Clean Up Australia Day.
40/2026.decisionSummary: Council recognises the volunteers who gave their time to local Clean Up Australia Day events.

83/2026.title: Transport Forum recommendations: March 2026
83/2026.description: Council’s decisions on the March Local Transport Forum and an April report outside the regular meeting cycle.
83/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts the recommendations of the 17 March 2026 Local Transport Forum and the report circulated on 2 April 2026.

81/2026.title: Community electric shuttle feasibility
81/2026.description: Costs, funding and demand for a possible Lane Cove community electric shuttle.
81/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to explore further funding and consult residents on two possible shuttle routes, with a report before the end of 2026 for the 2027/28 budget. It also continues lobbying for improved public buses, public ownership of Region 6 services and an on-demand service.

79/2026.title: Electric vehicle charging policy
79/2026.description: Council’s policy for electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
79/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts the amended Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Policy.

77/2026.title: 1 Austin Crescent heritage delisting proposal
77/2026.description: A planning proposal to remove the heritage listing at 1 Austin Crescent, Lane Cove.
77/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses the amended planning proposal for referral to the NSW planning department for Gateway approval. Public consultation is to follow Gateway requirements, and people who made informal submissions are to be advised.

75/2026.short: Financial hardship, investment and sister cities policies
75/2026.title: Financial hardship, investment and sister cities policies
75/2026.description: Council’s review of its financial hardship, investment and sister cities policies.
75/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts the Financial Hardship Policy, Investment Policy and Sister Cities Policy.

73/2026.title: Draft 2026/27 budget and Council plans
73/2026.description: Consultation on Council’s draft budget, fees, delivery program, operational plan and resourcing plans.
73/2026.decisionSummary: Council places the draft plans and fees on exhibition for six weeks, with results to return in June. It also places ward funds in a reserve for unfunded minor capital works and requires future funding requests through notices of motion, with staff to report on administration.

71/2026.short: Food scraps bins in existing strata buildings
71/2026.title: Food scraps bins in existing strata buildings
71/2026.description: Space and bin requirements for introducing food scraps collection to existing strata and multi-unit buildings.
71/2026.decisionSummary: Council defers the apartment rollout while it checks bin space and consults each building’s body corporate. It will monitor household general waste for six months, then review the number of general waste and food scraps bins needed for existing multi-unit buildings.

69/2026.title: Community CPR and defibrillator training
69/2026.description: Council participation in community CPR and automated external defibrillator training.
69/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to participate in the Heart Foundation’s training program, offer suitable venues, promote sessions and source equipment. It also requests advice on an accredited pathway for residents to become volunteer trainers.

113/2026.title: Fire Safety Policy consultation
113/2026.description: Community consultation on Council’s draft Fire Safety Policy.
113/2026.decisionSummary: Council places the draft Fire Safety Policy on public exhibition for 28 days and requests a report on the consultation results.

111/2026.title: Affordable Housing Policy consultation
111/2026.description: Proposed requirements for affordable housing contributions and the standard of dedicated dwellings.
111/2026.decisionSummary: Council places the amended Affordable Housing Policy on exhibition for six weeks. The draft target becomes “at least 10% where feasible”, and dedicated dwellings must have equivalent standards and access to shared facilities, entrances and exits.

109/2026.title: National Cultural Policy submission
109/2026.description: Council’s submission on Australia’s proposed National Cultural Policy.
109/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses its Culture, Community and Place submission and authorises the General Manager to lodge it with the Australian Government, with minor editorial changes if needed.

107/2026.title: Civic Art Collection Policy consultation
107/2026.description: Community consultation on a draft policy for Council’s civic art collection.
107/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses the draft Civic Art Collection Policy for six weeks of public exhibition. A further report is to cover submissions and recommended changes before adoption.

103/2026.title: Children and Families Strategy adoption
103/2026.description: Council’s adoption of its Children and Families Strategy.
103/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts the Children and Families Strategy and requests that its cover show the month and year of adoption.

101/2026.short: Internal Audit Charter and March committee minutes
101/2026.title: Internal Audit Charter and March committee minutes
101/2026.description: Council’s Internal Audit Charter and the March 2026 Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee minutes.
101/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes the draft committee minutes, which require no Council action, and adopts the Internal Audit Charter.

99/2026.title: 2025/26 Council plans: third-quarter review
99/2026.description: The third-quarter review of Council’s 2025/26 Delivery Program and Operational Plan.
99/2026.decisionSummary: Council receives and notes the third-quarter review of the 2025/26 Delivery Program and Operational Plan.

97/2026.short: Galuwa food, beverage and events lease
97/2026.title: Galuwa food, beverage and events lease
97/2026.description: Final approval of the food, beverage and events lease arrangements at Galuwa Recreation Centre.
97/2026.decisionSummary: Council authorises the General Manager to enter the head lease with SSMG on the proposed terms, including clause 29. It also approves the corresponding sublease for SSMG and Lusso to sign.

95/2026.title: Planning agreement: 177–183 Greenwich Road
95/2026.description: A planning agreement for 177–183 Greenwich Road, including oversight of improvement works.
95/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to enter the planning agreement, subject to an amendment requiring Council’s bushland coordinator to be consulted and oversee all stages of the improvement works. The General Manager may sign the necessary documents.

90/2026.short: Sports field allocation and open space use
90/2026.title: Sports field allocation and open space use
90/2026.description: Rules for allocating and managing sports fields while protecting other uses of public open space.
90/2026.decisionSummary: Council declines a full Open Space Plan review in 2026/27. Instead, it requests a report on transparent field allocation, shared use, maintenance, capacity, disputes and annual reporting, to return alongside the existing management directive review.

143/2026.short: Police advice on changing local crime trends
143/2026.title: Police advice on changing local crime trends
143/2026.description: Council’s request for police explanations of changes in assaults, malicious damage and property crime.
143/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes the report and agrees to ask North Shore Police Area Command why non-domestic assaults and malicious damage increased while property-related crime fell. It also seeks advice on the contribution of prevention initiatives and security technology.

141/2026.title: Habitat logs and wildlife refuges
141/2026.description: Reusing hollow logs from Council tree work and helping residents create wildlife habitat.
141/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses a habitat log salvage program for its bushland work and an initiative encouraging residents to use suitable materials from their property or Council’s log stockpile. It also supports partnerships for habitat-making and upcycling workshops.

139/2026.title: Submission on complying development changes
139/2026.description: Council’s response to proposed NSW complying development changes, including tree protection.
139/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses its submission on the proposed complying development changes. It adds a request for a Council arborist to approve development within three metres of a tree, rather than relying on an arborist paid by the applicant.

137/2026.title: Aquatic Centre electrification tender
137/2026.description: The tender for electrifying Lane Cove Aquatic Centre.
137/2026.decisionSummary: Council accepts Hirotec’s tender for the Aquatic Centre electrification upgrade. The General Manager is authorised to sign the contracts and approve variations within the approved budget.

135/2026.title: Peace Poles at The Canopy
135/2026.description: The proposed installation of Rotary Peace Poles near The Canopy’s lifts and stage.
135/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes the consultation results and endorses installing the Peace Poles beside the lifts behind The Canopy stage. Installation remains subject to final design, accessibility and operational approvals.

133/2026.title: Community and digital engagement consultation
133/2026.description: Consultation on Council’s draft community engagement policy, strategy and digital engagement strategy.
133/2026.decisionSummary: Council places the three draft engagement documents on exhibition for six weeks. The community engagement strategy must specify that exhibitions will not start between 15 December and 10 January inclusive, and consultation results are to be reported back.

131/2026.short: Ombudsman findings on Pottery Lane fire safety
131/2026.title: Ombudsman findings on Pottery Lane fire safety
131/2026.description: Council’s response to the NSW Ombudsman’s investigation of fire safety enforcement at 1–5 Pottery Lane.
131/2026.decisionSummary: Council accepts the Ombudsman’s findings and recommendations and formally apologises to Owners SP91522 for its unlawful and unreasonable actions, including enforcement failures and missing annual fire safety statements. It endorses the response and action plan, with a further report after implementation satisfies the Ombudsman.

129/2026.title: E-bike safety education
129/2026.description: Community education and advocacy on safe and lawful e-bike use.
129/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to seek stronger state education, enforcement and infrastructure support, and run a local safety campaign with youth and community engagement. Staff are to report within six months on actions, participation and further recommendations.

127/2026.title: Data centre regulation and compliance
127/2026.description: Council’s advocacy for stronger oversight of data centre construction, operations and community impacts.
127/2026.decisionSummary: Council seeks more state compliance resources, a single data centre regulator, clearer complaints processes and publicly available independent research on cumulative impacts. It agrees to raise these requests with state ministers and in relevant inquiries.

123/2026.title: Petition about funding drag events
123/2026.description: A petition concerning Council funding for drag events in Lane Cove.
123/2026.decisionSummary: Council receives and notes the petition.

121/2026.title: General Manager performance panel membership
121/2026.description: The membership term of the panel overseeing the General Manager’s performance review.
121/2026.decisionSummary: Council retains the existing performance review panel for the remainder of the Council term. Membership may change after the 2026/27 performance agreement is finalised if a vacancy arises or the full Council formally resets the panel for the next annual cycle.

117/2026.title: Reinstating Council’s earlier meeting code
117/2026.description: Changes to Council meeting rules after the NSW Parliament disallowed the 2025 model code regulation.
117/2026.decisionSummary: Council rescinds its December 2025 code decision and reinstates the code adopted in August 2025. Public forums remain at 7 pm on the Monday before ordinary meetings, with further consultation if a future code allows timing flexibility.

165/2026.title: Burns Bay Reserve masterplan consultation
165/2026.description: Community consultation on a draft masterplan for Burns Bay Reserve.
165/2026.decisionSummary: Council approves six weeks of exhibition for the draft Burns Bay Reserve Masterplan. The consultation material must explain that delivery may be staged, and the results are to be reported back.

163/2026.title: 2026 LGNSW conference attendance and delegates
163/2026.description: Councillor attendance, voting delegates and a proposed motion for the 2026 Local Government NSW conference.
163/2026.decisionSummary: Council authorises all councillors to attend the conference, dinner and women’s association breakfast. It appoints four voting delegates and four alternates, permits the Mayor to nominate replacements if needed, and endorses the proposed conference motion.

159/2026.short: Women in local government national conference
159/2026.title: Women in local government national conference
159/2026.description: Councillor attendance at the August 2026 Australian Local Government Women’s Association national conference.
159/2026.decisionSummary: Council approves attendance by Councillors Southwood, Greenwell and Little at the association’s 75th anniversary national conference.

157/2026.title: Data Breach Response Policy consultation
157/2026.description: Community consultation on how Council responds to data breaches.
157/2026.decisionSummary: Council places the Data Breach Response Policy on exhibition for six weeks and notes the associated management directive. A report on the consultation results is to follow.

155/2026.title: Protecting Badangi and Berrys Creek
155/2026.description: Proposed cooperation, pollution monitoring and compliance work to protect Badangi, including Berrys Creek.
155/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to explore joint work with North Sydney Council, support from Heritage NSW, a public pollution report register, development-site monitoring and Sydney Water communication. It also requests a review of enforcement powers and a report in October 2026.

152/2026.short: Joint advocacy for data centre reforms
152/2026.title: Joint advocacy for data centre reforms
152/2026.description: Council’s proposed participation in an international data centre pact and advocacy for a pause on new AI data centres.
152/2026.decisionSummary: Council authorises an expression of interest in the Global Urban Data Centres Pact. It will propose an LGNSW motion and write to federal ministers seeking a pause on new AI data centre projects until stronger planning, environmental and community protections are in place.

147/2026.title: 2026 Citizenship and Neighbour Day Awards
147/2026.description: Recognition of the recipients of Lane Cove’s 2026 Citizenship and Neighbour Day Awards.
147/2026.decisionSummary: Council acknowledges and congratulates the 2026 Lane Cove Citizenship and Neighbour Day Award recipients.

193/2026.title: Transport Forum recommendations: July 2026
193/2026.description: Council’s decision on recommendations from the July 2026 Local Transport Forum.
193/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts the recommendations of the Local Transport Forum held on 21 July 2026.

191/2026.title: Fire Safety Policy adoption
191/2026.description: Council’s adoption of its Fire Safety Policy after public consultation.
191/2026.decisionSummary: Council receives the report and adopts the Fire Safety Policy.

189/2026.title: Climate Emergency Plan consultation
189/2026.description: Consultation on the 2026–2030 Climate Emergency Plan and results of the previous Climate Resilience Plan.
189/2026.decisionSummary: Council places the draft Climate Emergency Plan and the 2021–2026 Climate Resilience Plan outcomes report on exhibition for 42 days. The consultation results are to return to Council.

187/2026.title: Events Management Policy adoption
187/2026.description: Council’s adoption of an Events Management Policy after public consultation.
187/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes the public exhibition results and adopts the Events Management Policy.

185/2026.short: Planning Agreements Policy and proposed fee
185/2026.title: Planning Agreements Policy and proposed fee
185/2026.description: Council’s rules for planning agreements and a proposed $5,000 application fee.
185/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopts the amended Planning Agreements Policy, requiring Council approval of agreement changes, and agrees to publish it. It also places a proposed $5,000 planning agreement application fee on exhibition for 28 days.

183/2026.title: Kindy Cove governance policies consultation
183/2026.description: Proposed governance and advisory committee policies for Kindy Cove Early Education and Care Service.
183/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes the policy review following NSW child safety reforms. It places the revised governance policy, appendices and management advisory committee policy on exhibition for six weeks, with a report on the results to follow.

181/2026.short: Community and digital engagement policies adoption
181/2026.title: Community and digital engagement policies adoption
181/2026.description: Council’s adoption of updated community engagement and digital communication policies and strategies.
181/2026.decisionSummary: Council notes the submissions and adopts its community engagement policy and strategy and its digital engagement, marketing and communications strategy. It makes two wording changes concerning families and the website search function.

179/2026.title: 2025/26 Council plans: fourth-quarter review
179/2026.description: The fourth-quarter review of Council’s 2025/26 Delivery Program and Operational Plan.
179/2026.decisionSummary: Council receives and notes the fourth-quarter review of the 2025/26 Delivery Program and Operational Plan.

175/2026.title: Shared e-bike parking and safety
175/2026.description: Parking standards, enforcement and community feedback for shared e-bikes in Lane Cove.
175/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to investigate more marked parking areas, explain reporting and parking rules, and report on compliance and liability. It will seek community feedback after the Lime trial and apply for a state grant to support parking and removal of obstructing bikes.

170/2026.short: Federal funding compact for local government
170/2026.title: Federal funding compact for local government
170/2026.description: Council’s response to federal commitments on local government grants, workforce and services.
170/2026.decisionSummary: Council welcomes the proposed Federation Compact and increased financial assistance grants. It agrees to write to federal leaders urging progress and thank Local Government NSW for its advocacy.

230/2026.short: Anglo Road reserve closure and sale
230/2026.title: Anglo Road reserve closure and sale
230/2026.description: A proposed closure and conditional sale of road reserve near Pacific Highway, retaining public pedestrian access.
230/2026.decisionSummary: Council authorises formal closure and conditional sale of the road reserve beside 126 and 130–134 Pacific Highway at an independently valued price. The sale requires development approval, lot consolidation and a registered public pedestrian access right; applicants must pay all costs.

228/2026.title: Burns Bay Reserve playground upgrades
228/2026.description: Delivery of playground upgrades at Burns Bay Reserve.
228/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to proceed with the Burns Bay Reserve playground upgrades.

225/2026.title: Vacant development site runoff controls
225/2026.description: Planning conditions for revegetating vacant development sites and limiting sediment runoff.
225/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to require revegetation and a landscaping plan where construction will not begin within six months of demolition. It also strengthens standard silt and erosion controls, including those approved in resolution 220/2025.

223/2026.title: 1 Austin Crescent planning proposal finalisation
223/2026.description: Final referral of the 1 Austin Crescent planning proposal after public consultation.
223/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses Planning Proposal 48 and sends it to the NSW planning department for finalisation. The General Manager is authorised to finalise the amendments.

221/2026.short: Community funding and grants policy consultation
221/2026.title: Community funding and grants policy consultation
221/2026.description: Consultation on community funding, subsidies, grants and assistance with cultural venue hire.
221/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses the draft Community Funding, Subsidies and Support Policy and two supporting grant guidelines for six weeks of exhibition. A further report is to cover submissions and recommended changes.

219/2026.short: Antisemitism and social cohesion summit attendance
219/2026.title: Antisemitism and social cohesion summit attendance
219/2026.description: Councillor attendance at the November 2026 Local Government Summit Against Antisemitism and for Social Cohesion.
219/2026.decisionSummary: Council approves registration for interested councillors at the 26–27 November summit, including Councillor Bennison, to allow registration before 30 September.

217/2026.title: 2026 LGNSW conference motions
217/2026.description: Council’s proposed conference motions on preschool funding, competitive neutrality and participation in development assessment.
217/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorses three LGNSW conference motions covering equitable preschool funding in long day care, modernising competitive neutrality requirements and community participation in development assessment. The General Manager may make minor wording changes without changing their intent.

1/2026.short: Smart glasses and recording devices in Council facilities
1/2026.title: Smart glasses and recording devices in Council facilities
1/2026.description: Privacy rules for wearable recording devices in sensitive areas of Council facilities, with disability and accessibility exemptions.
1/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to develop entry conditions regulating wearable recording devices in privacy-sensitive areas of its facilities. It requires accessibility exemptions, consultation with the Access and Age Friendly Advisory Committee, legal advice, practical enforcement procedures and periodic review.

213/2026.title: Urban fox management review
213/2026.description: A review of fox control, wildlife protection and practical advice for residents.
213/2026.decisionSummary: Council requests a review of fox control, including humane cage trapping, regional coordination, monitoring and help for residents. It also seeks updated public information and a report within four months on recommendations and possible trials, with attention to threatened wildlife.

209/2026.short: Cameraygal Wind Symphony state championship win
209/2026.title: Cameraygal Wind Symphony state championship win
209/2026.description: Recognition of Cameraygal Wind Symphony’s 2026 NSW State Band Championship win.
209/2026.decisionSummary: Council congratulates Cameraygal Wind Symphony on winning the Open B Grade Concert Band section and acknowledges its musicians and musical director Gavin Staines. It agrees to send a congratulatory letter.

202/2026.title: Internal committee appointments: 2026–2028
202/2026.description: Councillor appointments to internal committees through September 2028.
202/2026.decisionSummary: Council appoints councillors to its audit, selection, literary awards and transport committees for the period ending September 2028. All councillors serve on the selection committee, with named representatives and alternates on the other committees.

200/2026.title: Deputy Mayor election voting method
200/2026.description: The voting method for electing the Deputy Mayor.
200/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to elect the Deputy Mayor by a show of hands.

198/2026.title: Mayor election and voting method
198/2026.description: Arrangements for electing the Mayor for the term ending September 2028.
198/2026.decisionSummary: Council agrees to conduct the mayoral election for the term ending September 2028 under the applicable regulation, using a show of hands.
